summary: Careful, well-executed preregistered paired study measuring the marginal detection benefit of adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for LLM-produced NetOps artifacts. Execution and analysis appear faithful to the preregistration, artifacts are archived, and the paper responsibly bounds its conclusions. Main remaining defects are presentation/formatting and one disclosure/provenance wording issue that must be corrected before finalisation.
critical_issues: Disclosure Statement duplicates run-level provenance and per-file artifact bookkeeping in the main manuscript; per-track guidance requires a concise Disclosure inside the paper and relocation of detailed logs/hashes to the archived artifact bundle. This must be condensed.

Bibliographic formatting and citation semantics: the manuscript must use standard IEEE numbered references in prose and a conventional IEEE-style bibliography (no raw OpenAlex/DOI/arXiv URIs embedded in running text). Each numbered citation must correctly map to one of the verified terminal_bibliographic_records and must actually support the nearby scholarly claim. Resolve any ambiguous/misaligned reference markers using the archived reference records.

Ambiguous provider-call / audit field in deterministic_reconciliation: the manuscript presents provider_call_audit fields such as condition_counts:{"shared":720,"guarded":1} that are potentially confusing or misleading relative to episode accounting. The Methods must include a concise explicit explanation of these provider-audit fields (what “shared” vs “guarded” counts mean in the audit summary) or correct the transcription so the provenance statements are not misleading.
required_revisions: Condense the Disclosure Statement in the paper to a concise, human-readable summary that (a) lists LLM(s) and orchestration framework, (b) affirms the autonomy-lock and human role, (c) refers readers to the archived execution manifest for full hashes and per-file provenance. Do not reproduce execution logs, per-file inventories, or full hashes verbatim in the manuscript; instead cite the canonical artifact bundle and manifest path (as a single archival pointer).

Replace any raw repository/identifier strings in running prose with numbered IEEE citations and provide a standard IEEE-style bibliography. Ensure the three cited records in terminal_bibliographic_records are presented as numbered IEEE references and that each in-text citation ([1], [2], [3], etc.) corresponds to the correct bibliographic entry that supports the proximate claim. Fix any mismatches between in-text markers and bibliography entries.

Add a brief, explicit clarification in Methods describing provider-call audit fields and reconcile any apparent confusion (for example, explain the audited counts meaning and why stage_counts/provisioned condition_counts appear as shown). Use the archived execution artifacts to state the authoritative provenance facts; do not add new experiments.
optional_revisions: Add a one-paragraph, artifact-grounded description of the single discordant pair’s proximate cause (repair invocation vs emulation-only observation), referencing the archived raw_results.jsonl entry or pair_id without copying full logs into the paper.

Include a compact table summarizing task-difficulty strata (extreme/very_hard/hard/medium) and their sample counts to help readers interpret external validity; this table may be drawn verbatim from the archived difficulty_summary artifact.
Shorten and streamline Related Work to prioritize the closest prior empirical studies and a single-paragraph motivation tying them to the present paired design (helps keep the five-page limit).
